# Compaction

Compaction makes room in a long session by replacing older conversation with a summary, so the session can keep going past the modelâs context limit.

## How it works

When a session approaches the modelâs context limit, OpenCode summarizes the entire current conversation. It also keeps the most recent conversation, about 15,000 tokens by default, beside the summary so exact recent details remain available.

before [ system prompt ][ older conversation ............ ][ recent 15k ][ pending work ] request [ system prompt ][ older conversation ............ ][ recent 15k ][ summary instructions ] after [ system prompt ][ summary of older + recent ][ recent 15k ][ pending work ]

Sending the full conversation lets the summary request reuse the normal requestâs prompt cache when the provider supports it. Later compactions update the existing summary using the conversation since that checkpoint.

## Start

Automatic compaction is on by default:

{ "$schema" : "https://opencode.ai/config.json" , "compaction" : { "auto" : true , "keep" : { "tokens" : 15000 } , } , }

Compaction is lossy. Increase keep.tokens when exact recent details matter, or request compaction yourself before the automatic one.

## Manual

Request compaction at any time, even for a short history:

opencode api post /api/session/ses_example/compact --data '{}'

The api command discovers and authenticates with the background service. Its response confirms the request was accepted; it does not wait for the summary. Follow session.compaction.* events to learn when it finishes. See the API reference for the full operation.

Pass an id to make an exact retry idempotent. Reusing that ID for a different request returns a conflict.

opencode api post /api/session/ses_example/compact --data '{"id":"msg_compact_once"}'

## Settings

Add compaction to any OpenCode configuration file :

{ "$schema" : "https://opencode.ai/config.json" , "compaction" : { "auto" : false , "keep" : { "tokens" : 24000 } , "buffer" : "20%" , } , }

keep.tokens accepts a non-negative integer.

### Buffer

buffer is a percentage of each modelâs window, so one setting fits every model:

- It is the room kept free, not the point where compaction starts: "20%" compacts at 80% full.

- Accepts "1%" to "99%" , including decimals such as "12.5%" .

- A token count such as 20000 also works. The same count is a large share of a small window and a small share of a large one.

- A token count at least as large as the modelâs window is ignored and the default applies.

## Model

By default OpenCode writes the summary itself, using the sessionâs model. Set agents.compaction.model to use another model for summaries:

{ "$schema" : "https://opencode.ai/config.json" , "agents" : { "compaction" : { "model" : "anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5" } , } , }

If that model cannot be resolved, OpenCode falls back to the sessionâs model.

## Background compaction

OpenCode writes the summary ahead of time, while the session keeps going, and swaps it in when compaction is due. Automatic compaction then doesnât pause the session to write one:

60k tokens before the threshold summary of the conversation so far starts in the background the session keeps going; the summary is held, not applied threshold the held summary is swapped in; everything since it is kept as is

On small context windows, the summary starts at most halfway between the first response after the last compaction and the threshold.

Turn it off to write the summary only when compaction is due:

{ "$schema" : "https://opencode.ai/config.json" , "compaction" : { "background" : false , } , }

## Providers

Some providers can compact the conversation on their side instead. Enable it per provider or model with settings.compaction :

{ "$schema" : "https://opencode.ai/config.json" , "providers" : { "openai" : { "settings" : { "compaction" : { "type" : "native" } } , "models" : { "gpt-6.1-sol" : { "settings" : { "compaction" : { "type" : "summary" } } } , } , } , } , }

A model setting overrides the provider setting. native uses the providerâs compaction; summary uses OpenCodeâs own.

With native compaction, OpenCode sends the conversation to the providerâs compaction endpoint. The provider returns an opaque, encrypted item that stands in for the older conversation. Your recent messages and attachments, up to keep.tokens , are kept alongside it:

before [ older conversation ........................ ][ recent user messages ] after [ encrypted checkpoint + recent user messages ]

## Summaries

The summary is structured so another agent could pick the work up from it:

## Objective Finish the authentication migration. ## Next Move - Update the callback handler. - Verify the login flow.

It covers the objective and requirements, decisions, completed and active work, blockers and next moves, and relevant files. In the recent conversation kept beside it, long tool output is shortened and attachment data is replaced by a short description.

After compaction, the current versions of your instruction files become the sessionâs baseline; see Instructions .

## Limits

For example, compaction cannot help here:

128k context = 120k fixed instructions and tools + 8k conversation

## Migration

V1 used tail-turn and pruning behavior. V2 uses summaries and compaction.keep.tokens :

{ "compaction" : { "keep" : { "tokens" : 15000 } } }

The settings and behavior on this page apply to V2.

# Browse

An MCP server and a Chromium extension that let your agents use your real browser, with your tabs, your logins and your extensions. They open tabs in the background, grouped out of your way, and read pages, click, type, take screenshots and record tabs. When it's your turn, for a login, a 2FA prompt or a payment, they hand the tab back to you and continue once you click Continue.

- Your real browser Chrome, Edge, Brave, Arc, Helium, Vivaldi, Opera and Chromium.

- Out of your way Agent tabs open in the background, in collapsed groups.

- Handoffs Do the login or 2FA step yourself, then click Continue.

- Lend a tab Click the toolbar button to hand an agent a tab you have open.

- Record and capture Screenshots, tab recordings and network traffic.

- Any MCP client OpenCode, Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Zed and many more.

- All your logins Agents use the sites you're already signed into. No keys, no setup.

- Allowed sites Keep an agent's tab on the sites you name.

## Install

Install the Chrome extension first. It walks you through the rest of the steps. To install the CLI directly (you should not need to do this), use any of these.

- curl curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/browse/install | bash Copy curl command

- pwsh irm https://opencode.ai/browse/install.ps1 | iex Copy pwsh command

- npm npm install -g @opencode/browse && browse install Copy npm command

- bun bun add -g @opencode/browse && browse install Copy bun command
